title: Injury Q&A #1
summary: First injury-focused Q&A: NH covers shoulder pain on pullovers, triceps tendon pain from overdone French presses, what to do before training, scheduling presses twice a week without sore shoulders, and insomnia. He stresses knowing your joints, avoiding lockout and end-range abuse, and pairing horizontal with vertical presses.
claims: He is not a doctor and has no formal sport-science training; his injury knowledge comes from going through and fully rehabbing many injuries
Pullovers are a very important lat exercise; with pull-ups they are the two best lat exercises and high-volume pullovers transformed his lats
Pullovers made his chest look thicker from the front, whatever the truth of the rib-cage expansion claim
Shoulder pain on pullovers comes from heavy shoulder flexion; find your variation: dumbbell, EZ bar, plates, cable or band
Dumbbell pullovers put the hands close together which can internally rotate the shoulders; fine for narrow lifters like him, try an EZ bar if it hurts
Keep a slight elbow bend on pullovers to engage the long head and avoid overextending
Stop the pullover when the lat stops stretching; going further is just shoulder flexion and invites pain
Never go below 6 reps on pullovers; keep them light and high rep
Pain on pullovers often reveals overly tight shoulders from pressing rather than a problem with the pullover itself
The shoulder is very mobile but has weak ranges; loading those ranges snaps it, so learn exactly what your shoulder tolerates
Neutral-grip dumbbell pressing wrecks his shoulders while a straight bar with tucked elbows feels great
Learn every joint of your body; you will live in it for the rest of your life
Elbow tendon pain worse when cold and after training is tendinitis, likely from French presses going too deep or overextending at lockout
For tendon recovery try MSM powder, more water, more sleep and less stress, and ice 3 times a day for 10 minutes
Heal tendinitis by strengthening the surrounding muscle and its antagonist: include curls on triceps days
With tendinitis keep training but cut weight and stop locking out or fully extending; stop before the tendon starts rebounding the load
Rest alone won't fix tendinitis, and he advises against drugs for it
High-frequency, high-volume light triceps extensions push blood into the tendon and reteach form
Tendinitis becomes a tear only in people who ignore their body and keep pushing weight; low intensity windows keep you safe
Before training, be fed in your optimal window: not full and queasy, not hungry
Warm up with movements replicating your heavy patterns until you sweat, get a pump or feel warm; it's not rocket science
Don't reduce horizontal press volume to save sore shoulders; rotate variations like close-grip bench, football bar, push-ups and band flyes
End a heavy bench day with a heavy overhead press; it barely hurts progress and makes shoulders feel amazing
When his shoulders were a problem, heavy overhead pressing after bench made them feel fine
Hitting everything twice a week usually needs a 6-day program with three upper days
Don't repeat heavy horizontal presses too often; that's what makes shoulders sore
Always do face pulls and rear delt flyes to protect the rotator cuff
Insomnia is often a vicious circle: tired mornings lead to caffeine abuse, which wrecks sleep and overtaxes the adrenals
Insomnia can be stress, genetic or hormonal, and anxiety about not sleeping makes it worse
exercises: slight elbow bend; stop when lat stops stretching; >=6 reps
top lat builder; shoulder pain if overreaching
don't go too deep or lock out
Close-grip bench / football bar bench / push-ups / band flyes
